headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia’s broad network egress can leak or amplify content if paired with a documentation-only writer, but no shared write channel or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between authelia and python-cheatsheet: authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, file mount, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess for injection.
IF authelia begins parsing untrusted file or API content as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard and shared filesystem.
Route any exchanged text through a sanitizer that strips instruction-like markup.
Review any future MCP or API bridge before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes or filesystem surfaces. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow, so leakage is limited to unusual integration rather than default operation.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF authelia is configured to process secrets or PII, reassess for higher impact.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace between the agents.
Keep secrets out of any content passed to authelia.
Verify outbound destinations for authelia before deployment.
Use separate service accounts and credentials.
requires-engineering: add egress allowlisting for authelia.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no write or shell capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource or concurrency surface in the profiles, so capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess for conflict.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared assets.
Avoid placing them under the same writable working tree.
Document any future shared resource before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is a reference/documentation agent, so it is unlikely to act on authelia’s outputs. Authelia can emit authentication-related responses, but there is no documented pipeline where B treats A’s output as authoritative or takes downstream actions, making cascading error possible only through unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is wired to render or execute authelia-generated text without review, reassess upward.
IF authelia outputs are used as policy inputs, reassess for higher impact.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action based on authelia output.
Keep python-cheatsheet in read-only documentation mode.
Do not auto-commit or auto-send content derived from authelia.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for any downstream consumer.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched and no secrets handled. With no compliance-sensitive data flow identified, there is no evidenced residency or retention mismatch to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, reassess compliance.
IF a residency or retention policy is later documented and differs between agents, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency before any production use.
Review vendor policies if either agent begins handling PII.
